_: The gardener. THE CHANNEL'S FIRST HUMAN CHARACTER, drawn for jt-monkey-gardener.
docs/03 flagged this as a decision rather than a detail, and it is: an ORDINARY man on
an Indian children's channel has to carry docs/01's rule about crowds -- nobody a
caricature, nobody a type -- on his own, because there is no crowd to be various in.
So he is drawn as one specific, unremarkable person: middle-aged, working, tired, kind.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and each of these is a way of turning a person into a type:
- no caste marker of any kind, and no janeu
- no religious mark -- no tilak, no cap, no cross, no thread beyond a plain one
- no exaggerated features, no comic nose, no comic belly, no bare-toothed grin
- no rags: he is poor and he is not a costume
- and no bare chest with a grey beard: that silhouette reads as a sage, and this
channel does not put a religious figure on screen by accident. He wears a plain
He is north Indian because the Jataka is, and the story does not say more than that.
A gardener, a farmer, a potter and a merchant are the same four people in two hundred
of the app's stories, so this cell is a fixed cost of the channel and not of one film.
A HUMAN SHOULD LOOK AT THIS SHEET before any film using it is published. It is the one
asset in the library where the editorial call is not the pipeline's to make alone.

cells.gardener-water: An ordinary middle-aged Indian man, a working gardener, FULL BODY, in three-quarter view facing LEFT, stooping forward to pour water from a round clay pot held in both hands. Warm brown skin, short black hair going grey at the temples, a short greying beard, plain undyed cotton: a simple short-sleeved knee-length kurta over a dhoti to mid-calf, and a thin cloth folded over one shoulder, bare feet. Kind tired eyes, a small closed smile, unexaggerated ordinary features. NO turban, NO jewellery, NO caste or religious mark of any kind, NO bare chest, NO comic exaggeration. IN THE SAME HAND AS THE REFERENCE ANIMALS: thick soft warm-brown outlines of the SAME WEIGHT as the monkey's, FLAT CEL SHADING ONLY -- no gradients, no airbrushing, no gloss, no shine on the skin, no rendered muscle. Simplified picture-book cartoon proportions, a slightly large head, simple hands, soft rounded shapes. He must look as though the same artist drew him and the monkey on the same afternoon. Children's picture-book cartoon, NOT a stock vector illustration.
